stories.title: Nessel and green groups challenge DTE power deals for Saline data centers
stories.dek: Environmental groups and Attorney General Dana Nessel are appealing contracts that would let DTE supply power to large data centers in Saline Township. The outcome could affect electric rates and grid reliability for Washtenaw County residents. The appeal centers on whether the deals properly protect ratepayers from the massive new load.
stories.source_title: Environmental groups, Nessel make arguments in appeal of DTE Energy's Saline Township data center contracts - Planet Detroit

stories.title: Ypsilanti Township vows fight against UM's $1.2B Huron River data center
stories.dek: University of Michigan has picked a Huron River site in Ypsilanti Township for a major computing facility. Township officials say they will oppose the project over concerns about water use, traffic, and local control. Residents 30 miles away could see indirect effects on regional power demand and tax base.
stories.source_title: University of Michigan confirms Huron River site for $1.2 billion computing facility: Ypsilanti Township vows to fight back - Planet Detroit

stories.title: Morley delays hydro data center hearing to Aug 18
stories.dek: Morley officials pushed back a meeting on a proposed hydro-powered data center. Residents near the site want details on power use, water draw and tax impact before any vote. The delay gives locals more time to review plans that could reshape the small Mecosta County community.
stories.source_title: Morley reschedules hydro-powered data center meeting for Aug. 18 - Midland Daily News

stories.title: Wixom tightens data center rules before 6-month moratorium ends
stories.dek: Wixom officials are drafting new zoning and performance standards for data centers as the temporary ban expires. Residents in Oakland County worry about noise, power strain and water use from large facilities. The rules could set the template for other suburbs facing similar proposals.
stories.source_title: Wixom city council takes steps to regulate data centers as 6-month moratorium nears end - WXYZ Channel 7

stories.title: State Sen. Gonzalez starts tour pushing data center rules
stories.dek: Senator Gonzalez is holding public stops across Michigan to build support for tighter oversight of new AI facilities. The tour highlights risks to electric reliability and water supplies in rural and suburban areas where projects are proposed. Residents get a direct chance to weigh in before more campuses get approved.
stories.source_title: Senator Gonzalez Launches Statewide Tour Supporting Responsible AI Data Center Development - Harlem World Magazine

stories.title: East Lansing extends data center freeze another year, blocking new proposals
stories.dek: City Council voted to keep the moratorium in place, preventing any new data center applications from moving forward. Residents 30 miles away in the Lansing region face the same risk of sudden power and water strain if large facilities land nearby. The extension keeps local zoning rules unchanged while the city studies long-term impacts.
stories.source_title: East Lansing City Council votes to extend the data center moratorium - WILX

stories.title: U-M regent urges pause on Ypsilanti Twp data center over grid strain
stories.dek: A University of Michigan regent called for a temporary halt to the proposed data center in Ypsilanti Township. The move highlights concerns about electricity demand and local infrastructure costs. Nearby communities could see rate hikes if the project advances without new power safeguards.
stories.source_title: University of Michigan Regent calls for pause of proposed data center in Ypsilanti Twp. - FOX 2 Detroit

stories.title: Kalamazoo commissioners set to decide six-month data center ban
stories.dek: City leaders will vote on extending the moratorium, which would halt all new proposals for half a year. The move directly affects Kalamazoo County residents worried about electricity costs and industrial-scale water withdrawals. A yes vote would give the city time to write permanent rules before any project advances.
stories.source_title: Kalamazoo city commissioners to vote on data center moratorium - WWMT

stories.title: Michigan AG challenges OpenAI-Oracle data center deal over costs to ratepayers
stories.dek: Attorney General Dana Nessel is pushing back on a proposed OpenAI and Oracle data center arrangement. The move targets potential spikes in electricity bills for Michigan households. Lawmakers and utilities will now face added scrutiny on any large power contracts.
stories.source_title: Michigan AG takes aim at OpenAI, Oracle data center deal - MLex

stories.title: Corunna adopts rules to steer future data center projects
stories.dek: The new ordinance sets zoning and review standards for any proposed data centers. Residents in Shiawassee County now have clearer limits on where and how large facilities could be built. The rules aim to protect local infrastructure and tax base.
stories.source_title: Corunna ordinance regulates potential data centers - WJRT ABC12

stories.title: UM locks in Textile Road for $1.2B Los Alamos supercomputer campus
stories.dek: The University of Michigan chose the Textile Road site in Pittsfield Township for a massive high-performance computing facility tied to Los Alamos. The project will draw heavy power and water loads in Washtenaw County and reshape local land use. Residents 30 miles away will feel the effects through utility rates and traffic changes.
stories.source_title: University of Michigan selects Textile Road site for $1.2B Los Alamos supercomputing facility - mlive.com

national.title: Data centers advance rapidly as regulators scramble for rules
national.dek: Across the U.S., officials race to impose guardrails on power-hungry facilities while communities push back on incentives and impacts.
